title: Dual-path end-to-end metering audit for batched vs streamed requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need an end-to-end audit and corrective plan for the metering pipeline that handles two diverging request paths: (1) batched synchronous requests routed through the batcher + kernel-level token counters and (2) streaming/chunked requests that emit partial token attributions over websocket/HTTP-stream. Recent customer reports and periodic reconciliations show small but persistent billing deltas tied to retry/resume scenarios and mixed workloads where batching and streaming touch shared KV/prefix caches. This ticket captures investigation, invariant definition, instrumentation gaps, fixes, and rollout steps.
technical_design: Overview: current pipeline splits at the ingress layer into 'batch' and 'stream' flows. Both land eventual token attributions into the metering ledger service (billing-ledger). Problems found so far: lack of a single canonical meter_event_id per logical request, streaming chunk idempotency not enforced, partial-attribution not reconciled on retry, and batch mergers that reassign prefix tokens to downstream merged requests. Design goals: (1) establish a canonical request-level meter_id propagated through batcher, streamer, and runtime; (2) attach per-chunk sequence numbers and a checksum for idempotency; (3) make the reconciler able to collapse duplicate chunk attributions and handle 'resume' semantics by using last-seen sequence number and watermark; (4) ensure prefix/KV cache attributions are recorded as separate ledger line-items tagged with cache_hit=true and linked to the originating meter_id; (5) extend ledger schema with optional fields: meter_id, chunk_seq, chunk_checksum, cache_hit, attribution_phase. Backward compatibility: new fields are optional; older rows without meter_id still accepted. Reconciler will run in 'shadow' mode initially comparing old vs new attribution totals before switching billing to new ledger lines.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming session for a long generation and intentionally cause a network disconnect after N tokens, then resume the stream from the client using resume token. Observe duplicate/overcounted tokens in billing ledger.

2) Send multiple small synchronous requests that the batcher merges into a single GPU batch and then sample per-request attributions; compare token counts assigned to individual requests vs kernel-level token output.
3) Simulate model fallback (A->B) mid-stream: ensure token attribution for prefix tokens from failed model and restarted model are not double-billed.
4) Run concurrent mixed workload where cached prefix is hit for some requests and missed for others; verify cache_hit ledger tags and that merged batch attribution splits cache credits correctly.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical meter_id is generated at ingress and is present on >99.9% of newly written ledger rows for both batch and stream flows.
Streaming chunks include sequence numbers and the reconciler can dedupe attributions on duplicate chunk arrivals (proven by end-to-end test harness).
Reconciler shadow run shows cumulative billing delta <= 0.02% compared to historical baseline for a 24h mixed workload; any deviations are explained by known edge cases in a runbook.
Dashboard panels added: per-meter_id token stream (sampled), chunk duplication rate, cache_hit attribution rate, and post-reconcile reconciliation_delta alerting.
No customer-facing billing changes during shadow period; only after QA signoff do we flip billing read to new ledger attribution.
test_plan: Unit tests: meter_id propagation through batcher, streamer, runtime wrappers; chunk idempotency checks; ledger row schema migrations.

Integration harness: synthetic client that drives mixed workload (50% streamed long gen, 50% batched short gen) with injected disconnects and retries. Compare 'ground truth' token counter inside harness to ledger totals.
Property-based tests: random sequences of disconnects/resumes/retries ensuring reconciler invariants hold (monotonic per-request attribution once resume acknowledged).
Load test: 1h@p95 traffic replay from production trace (anonymized) in staging with reconciler shadow on, measure performance impact and memory of reconciler state.
Chaos test: kill batcher worker mid-batch and ensure reconcilers do not double-attribute merged-batch tokens to multiple request IDs.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement ledger schema changes behind feature flag 'meter_v2'.
2) Instrument batcher and streamer to attach meter_id and chunk metadata; deploy to staging and run integration harness.
3) Deploy reconciler in shadow mode against production traffic for 72h, capture reconciliation deltas and investigate any outliers.
4) If shadow metrics stable and delta < acceptance threshold, enable new billing read path for non-critical customers (canary 5% orgs) for 48h and monitor.
5) Full flip: enable for all hosted customers, keep reconciler shadowing for 7 days, then retire old reconciler logic after 30 days once no regressions.
links: Support ticket: https://redwood.support/tickets/PROD-4521 (customer report of duplicate stream charges)
comments: 2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after initial post-mortem; baseline reconciliations show ~0.05% drift concentrated in streaming retry/resume windows.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Liu: Spike-profiling shows reconciler memory grows with number of unique meter_ids; investigating lightweight watermarking strategy. Next step: prototype chunk_seq retention policy.
2026-03-08 - Design review: Added requirement to surface cache_hit as explicit ledger tag to make prefix accounting auditable. Action: ENG infra to add cache tagging in 2 days.
2026-03-11 - Marcus Liu: Implemented prototype instrumentation in staging. Early tests show duplicate chunk arrivals reduced when producer-side checksum is enabled; need end-to-end determinism tests.

2026-03-14 - QA: Running 24h shadow run in staging with anonymized production trace. Observed two outliers where model fallback doubled attribution for 1 request. Root cause: fallback path failed to propagate original meter_id; hotfix in PR #7901.
